bib.title: Sparse Modeling and the Lasso (Computer Age Statistical Inference, ch. 16)

question: How do we select and shrink variables in wide-data regression, and how do stepwise selection, the lasso and LARS relate and get computed?
contributions: Reviews best-subset and forward-stepwise regression, the lasso, LAR as exact path algorithm, pathwise coordinate descent for generalized lasso, post-selection inference, and links to SVM and boosting

limits: Chapter says it is mostly about prediction, with little attention to inference (p. 317).
Spam-data timings and fits come from 2015 software and hardware, unspecified beyond the 6 s figure.
Post-selection inference is a brief survey; HIV example supplied by Tibshirani and shown only as a figure.
Lasso has difficulty choosing among highly correlated predictors (motivates elastic net, p. 316).
LAR path coincides with lasso only with a drop-variable modification; dropping tends to occur with highly correlated variables (p. 312).
practices: Standardize predictors to variance one before the lasso because the l1 constraint treats coefficients equally (p. 305-306).
Choose subset size or lambda by K-fold cross-validation (K=10), scoring on the metric you care about, e.g. misclassification, even if fitting used squared error (p. 300, 302).
Do not restrict the intercept in the lasso (p. 306, fn 3).
Use warm starts, active-set iteration and strong rules for pathwise coordinate descent (p. 314-316).
Use the elastic net when predictors are highly correlated (p. 316).
Naive CIs after lasso selection ignore selection; use selection-adjusted intervals (p. 318-319).
